The table below is cross-checked against what's actually installed in the project's `venv/` and what each package is actually imported for in the code.

| Dependency | Purpose | Used in | Verified actually imported? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fastapi` | Web framework — defines HTTP routes | [main.py](../main.py) | Yes |
| `uvicorn` | The actual server process that runs the FastAPI app | run from the command line, not imported in code | Yes (as a CLI tool) |
| `openai` | SDK for calling OpenRouter's OpenAI-compatible API | [pipeline.py](../pipeline.py), [advisor.py](../advisor.py), [embedder.py](../embedder.py) | Yes |
| `python-dotenv` | Loads `.env` into environment variables | same three files above | Yes (imported as `dotenv`) |
| `numpy` | Vector math (cosine similarity) | [retriever.py](../retriever.py) | Yes |
| `fastmcp` | Builds the MCP tool server | [mcp_server/server.py](../mcp_server/server.py) | Yes |
| `httpx` | HTTP client, used server-side to fetch an image by URL | [mcp_server/server.py](../mcp_server/server.py) | Yes |
| `pillow` | Listed in the README's install command | — | **No — not imported anywhere in the codebase.** This appears to be a leftover from an earlier plan (perhaps for image validation/processing) that was never implemented, or a copy-paste artifact in the README. Flagged as a documentation inaccuracy. |

None of these packages have pinned version numbers recorded anywhere in the repo — the exact versions currently installed (from the active `venv/`) are `fastapi 0.141.1`, `fastmcp 3.4.7`, `httpx 0.28.1`, `numpy 2.2.6`, `openai 3.2.0`, `python-dotenv 1.2.3`, `uvicorn 0.52.4`. Without a lock file, a fresh `pip install` on a new machine could pull different (potentially incompatible) versions in the future.

## 15. Error Handling

| Failure scenario | What actually happens | Where in the code |
|---|---|---|
| Uploaded file isn't an image (`/analyze-report` or `/upload`) | Immediate `HTTPException(400, "...")`, checked via `file.content_type.startswith("image/")` — note this trusts a client-supplied header, it does not inspect the actual file bytes | [main.py](../main.py) |
| A vision model call fails or returns bad JSON | Caught by a broad `except Exception`, recorded as `last_error`, next attempt/model is tried. If every model/attempt in `VISION_MODELS` fails, the last exception is re-raised | `extract_biomarkers()` in [pipeline.py](../pipeline.py) |
| A text-generation call fails | Same pattern, but with a real sleep-based backoff (`attempt * 5` seconds) between retries, since these failures are more often genuine rate-limit congestion | `call_model_with_fallback()` in [advisor.py](../advisor.py) |
| An embedding call fails | Its own independent retry loop, 3 attempts, same backoff style; re-raises on the final failure | `embed_text()` in [embedder.py](../embedder.py) |
| The pipeline raises for any reason, via the REST route | Caught in `main.py`'s `try/except Exception as e:`, turned into `HTTPException(500, detail=f"Analysis failed: {str(e)}")` — the temp file is still deleted via `finally` regardless | [main.py](../main.py) |
| The pipeline raises for any reason, via the MCP tool | **Not caught anywhere in `mcp_server/server.py`.** The exception propagates up into FastMCP's own request handling, which is responsible for converting it into an MCP-level error the calling AI client sees. There's no custom, human-readable error message crafted for this path the way there is for the REST path — a real asymmetry between the two entry points (see [Section 23](#23-code-quality-strengths-risks--improvement-opportunities)) | [mcp_server/server.py](../mcp_server/server.py) |
| The MCP tool is given a URL that doesn't point to a real image (bad URL, 404, non-image content) | `httpx.get(...).raise_for_status()` will raise on a non-2xx response and stop immediately. If the URL *does* return 200 but the bytes aren't actually a valid image, there's no check for this — the bytes get written to a `.png` file regardless, and the failure only surfaces later, inside Stage 1, when the vision model can't make sense of it | [mcp_server/server.py](../mcp_server/server.py) |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` missing/invalid | Not checked proactively anywhere — the first real AI call will simply fail with an authentication error from OpenRouter, which then flows through the same retry/fallback/500 path as any other AI failure | implicit, via any OpenRouter call |

## 16. Logging & Debugging

There is **no logging framework** used anywhere in this codebase — every diagnostic message is a plain `print(...)` statement (e.g. `print(f"Trying model: {model} (attempt {attempt})...")`). This means: no log levels (info/warning/error), no structured/JSON logs, and no way to filter verbosity — everything printed goes straight to whatever terminal is running `uvicorn`. This is explicitly called out as a known gap in the project's own roadmap ("Structured logging in place of `print()` statements").

**A practical way to debug an issue in this app, adapted to how it's actually built:**

```
Something went wrong
   ↓
Check the terminal running `uvicorn main:app` — every retry/fallback attempt
prints a line (e.g. "Trying model: X (attempt N)..." / "Failed (...)").
   ↓
Was it a REST call? Check for the HTTPException status/detail in the response —
main.py always includes the real exception message in a 500's "detail" field.
   ↓
Was it an MCP/ChatGPT call? There's no equivalent friendly message — check the
raw server logs directly for the real Python exception, since it isn't
reformatted before reaching the AI client.
   ↓
Is MOCK_AI accidentally "true"? That would explain a result that looks static
or ignores the actual uploaded image.
   ↓
Is this a "used to work" regression after a restart? Check `which python3` —
the recurring root cause throughout this project's history has been a
deactivated venv in a fresh terminal (see LEARNING_JOURNAL.md — hit at least
three separate times).
   ↓
Is it specifically a ChatGPT/MCP mismatch (wrong arguments sent)? ChatGPT can
cache an old tool schema after the tool's parameters change — removing and
re-adding the connector (not just toggling it) forces a fresh schema fetch.
```

## 17. Testing

**There are no automated tests anywhere in this repository** — no `pytest`, no test files, no CI configuration. This is confirmed by the repo's file listing (no `test_*.py` or `tests/` directory exists) and matches the project's own roadmap, which lists "Proper testing (pytest)" as not yet started.

What currently substitutes for testing:
- **`playground.py`** — a manual scratch script for poking at retrieval behavior.
- **`pipeline.py`'s `if __name__ == "__main__":` block** — running `python3 pipeline.py` is a manual, human-observed smoke test of the whole pipeline against `sample_report.png`.
- **`MOCK_AI=true`** — lets a human manually exercise the entire REST/MCP plumbing (uploads, routing, response shape) with zero real network calls, though this only proves the *plumbing* works, not that the AI logic itself produces correct results.
- **MCP Inspector** (`npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector ...`) — a manual, browser-based tool for triggering the MCP tool directly, used during development of `mcp_server/server.py`.
- **The actual ChatGPT connector** — the most "real" end-to-end validation performed so far, done manually and once (documented in the README's MCP section), not something that runs repeatably.

Not covered by anything today: automated verification that `categorize()` produces correct High/Low/Normal tags, that `chunk_text()` splits correctly at edge cases (e.g. text shorter than one chunk), that the fallback loops actually move to the next model after real failures, or that the API's error responses have the right shape.

## 18. Running the Application

These are the exact, verified commands — matching what the code and `.env` actually expect (port `8001`, not the `8000`/`8005` you may see in older references).

**1. Set up the environment**
```bash
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate      # on Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
pip install fastapi uvicorn openai python-dotenv numpy fastmcp httpx
```
(`pillow`, listed in the README, is not actually required by any code — see [Section 14](#14-dependencies).)

**2. Configure `.env`** (repo root)
```bash
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=your-openrouter-key-here
MOCK_AI=true
BACKEND_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8001
```
Start with `MOCK_AI=true` for your first run — it costs nothing and proves the plumbing works before spending any real AI quota.

**3. Build the knowledge base** (only needed once, or after editing `articles/`)
```bash
python3 build_vector_store.py
```

**4. Start the server**
```bash
uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8001
```

**5. Verify it's running**
```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/
# {"status": "Blood Report Analyser API is running"}
```

**6. Try the real endpoint**
```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8001/analyze-report -F "file=@sample_report.png"
```

**7. (Optional) Test the CLI pipeline directly, without the server**
```bash
python3 pipeline.py
```

**8. (Optional) Expose it publicly for an AI assistant like ChatGPT**
```bash
ngrok http 8001
```
Register `https://<ngrok-subdomain>.ngrok-free.dev/mcp` as the MCP connector URL in ChatGPT's connector settings. Remember: this free ngrok URL changes every time the tunnel restarts, and (per [Section 13](#13-configuration--environment)) there is currently no authentication on this endpoint at all while it's exposed.

## 19. Complete Practical Example

This traces one real, already-verified request end to end (the exact scenario documented in the README, run in `MOCK_AI=true` mode).

```
User has a blood report photo, wants ChatGPT to analyze it
    ↓
[B1] curl -X POST https://<ngrok>/upload -F "file=@report.png"
     → main.py: upload_report() saves it as uploads/0cd76a6d-....png
     → returns {"url": "/uploads/0cd76a6d-....png"}
    ↓
[B2] User, in ChatGPT: "Analyze this blood report using the Blood Report
     Analyser tool: https://<ngrok>/uploads/0cd76a6d-....png"
    ↓
[B3] ChatGPT (its own reasoning, outside this repo) decides to call:
     analyze_blood_report(image_url="https://<ngrok>/uploads/0cd76a6d-....png")
    ↓
[B4] Request arrives at .../mcp on the ngrok tunnel → forwarded to
     localhost:8001/mcp → routed by FastMCP to analyze_blood_report()
    ↓
[B5] mcp_server/server.py: httpx.get(...) fetches the image bytes itself,
     writes them to a temp .png file
    ↓
[B6] pipeline.analyze_report(tmp_path) runs:
     - Stage 1 (MOCK_AI=true): returns MOCK_BIOMARKERS immediately, no AI call
     - Stage 2: categorize() flags Hemoglobin 10.6 → Low, Hematocrit 38.2% →
       Low, Total Leukocyte Count 13.8 → High, Platelet Count 128 → Low
       (compared against reference_ranges.py's min/max table)
     - Stage 3+4 (MOCK_AI=true): returns MOCK_ADVICE immediately, no AI call
    ↓
[B7] Result: {"biomarkers": {...}, "categorized": {...}, "advice": "This is
     placeholder advice generated in MOCK_AI mode..."} returned as the tool
     result, back through /mcp, through ngrok, to ChatGPT
    ↓
[B8] ChatGPT renders this as a conversational answer: a table of the four
     abnormal results with their reference ranges and status, a bulleted
     list of normal values, a "what this may indicate" explanation (anemia
     pattern given normal MCV, elevated WBC possibly infection/inflammation/
     stress, mild thrombocytopenia), and a closing recommendation to discuss
     with a doctor — correctly noting the data came from mock/test mode.
```

Every file/function named above is exactly what runs — nothing in this example is hypothetical.

## 20. How to Read This Codebase

Recommended order for a new developer, and why:

```
1. README.md               — the project's own framing of what it is and how to run it
2. LEARNING_JOURNAL.md       — the "why," in the original author's own words, including
                                every real bug hit and how it was diagnosed
3. main.py                    — the actual entry point; see where routes are defined
                                 and how the MCP server gets mounted in
4. pipeline.py                  — the single function that ties every stage together;
                                    read this before any individual stage file
5. categorize.py + reference_ranges.py — the simplest stage; a good warm-up before
                                           the AI-heavy stages
6. advisor.py + retriever.py + embedder.py — the RAG stages, in the order data
                                               actually flows through them
7. chunker.py + load_articles.py + build_vector_store.py — the offline prep step
                                                              that produces vector_store.json
8. mcp_server/server.py           — now that you know what analyze_report() does,
                                      see how it's exposed as an AI-callable tool
9. mock_data.py                    — small, but explains what "MOCK_AI=true" actually
                                       changes at each stage
10. This document (LEARNING.md)     — cross-check your understanding against it
```

Why this order: it follows the same path a real request actually takes (entry point → orchestrator → each stage in execution order → the offline prep behind Stage 3 → the second entry point that reuses everything). Reading `mcp_server/server.py` before `pipeline.py` would leave you looking at `analyze_report(tmp_path)` with no idea what it does yet.

## 21. Learning Journey & Architectural Decisions

This section connects specific entries in `LEARNING_JOURNAL.md` to exactly where their outcome lives in the code today.

**Decision: rule-based code instead of AI for categorization**
- *Why it was needed:* every extracted biomarker value needs a High/Low/Normal tag.
- *Options considered:* ask an AI model to make the call, vs. plain code comparing against a table.
- *Chosen approach:* plain code — `categorize.py` + `reference_ranges.py`.
- *Why:* comparing a number to a range has exactly one correct answer; using an AI model for a deterministic task adds cost, latency, and needless risk of error with zero upside.
- *Trade-off:* the reference table must be manually maintained and only covers biomarkers someone explicitly added; anything else is tagged "Unknown."
- *Where implemented:* [categorize.py](../categorize.py), [reference_ranges.py](../reference_ranges.py).

**Decision: a flat JSON file instead of a real vector database**
- *Why it was needed:* Stage 3 needs somewhere to store and search article-chunk embeddings.
- *Options considered:* a managed vector database (Pinecone, Chroma, etc.) vs. a plain JSON file plus manual cosine similarity.
- *Chosen approach:* the JSON file (`vector_store.json`) + `retriever.py`'s from-scratch similarity search.
- *Why:* this is a learning project — the goal was to *see* the retrieval mechanics directly (embed, compare, sort, return top-k) instead of having a library hide them.
- *Trade-off:* a full linear scan over every chunk on every query; fine at ~50 chunks, would not scale to a large knowledge base.
- *Where implemented:* [retriever.py](../retriever.py), generated by [build_vector_store.py](../build_vector_store.py).

**Decision: `image_url` instead of `image_base64` for the MCP tool**
- *Why it was needed:* the original `image_base64: str` tool signature caused ChatGPT's client to hang indefinitely while base64-encoding an 83KB image — it never even reached the server.
- *Options considered:* MCP's native `ImageContent` type (rejected — documented as not rendering correctly in ChatGPT at the time); a `file://` local path (rejected — assumes client and server share a filesystem, which is false for a remote/cloud AI host reaching a server over ngrok).
- *Chosen approach:* a new `POST /upload` endpoint returns a URL; the tool takes that URL and fetches the bytes itself, server-side, via `httpx`.
- *Why:* no binary data ever has to pass through an MCP tool argument at all — only a short string does.
- *Where implemented:* [main.py](../main.py)'s `/upload` route, [mcp_server/server.py](../mcp_server/server.py)'s `httpx.get(...)`.

**Decision: merge the MCP server into the main FastAPI backend**
- *Why it was needed:* once the MCP tool needed to fetch images from a *publicly reachable* URL (ChatGPT correctly refuses to fetch `127.0.0.1` addresses), both the backend and the MCP server needed to be tunneled — but ngrok's free tier only allows **one active tunnel at a time** (`ERR_NGROK_334` was hit when a second was attempted).
- *Options considered:* pay for a second ngrok tunnel, vs. combine both services into one process/port.
- *Chosen approach:* mount the FastMCP app inside the FastAPI app (`app.mount("/mcp", mcp_app)`), sharing one Uvicorn process and one ngrok tunnel.
- *Trade-off:* the two services are now coupled to the same deploy/restart lifecycle — you can no longer restart just the MCP layer independently. This is also **why** `mcp_server/server.py`'s old standalone `if __name__ == "__main__":` entry point became dead code and was subsequently removed (see [6.2](#62-mcp_serverserverpy--the-mcp-tool-server)).
- *Where implemented:* [main.py](../main.py).

**Decision: `MOCK_AI` flag for cost-free development**
- *Why it was needed:* real AI calls cost quota (OpenRouter's free tier caps at 50 requests/day per account, shared across every model), and iterating on plumbing (uploads, routing, response shape) doesn't need real AI output every time.
- *Chosen approach:* a single environment variable, checked at the top of `extract_biomarkers()` and `analyze_report()`, swapping in `mock_data.py`'s canned values.
- *Where implemented:* [pipeline.py](../pipeline.py), [mock_data.py](../mock_data.py).

**Observation (not a documented decision, but visible directly in the code): three separate `OpenAI` client instances**
- `pipeline.py`, `advisor.py`, and `embedder.py` each independently create their own `OpenAI(base_url=..., api_key=...)` client and call `load_dotenv()` themselves, rather than sharing one client/config module. This isn't called out as a deliberate decision anywhere in the journal — it reads as organic growth (each file was built and tested somewhat independently) rather than an intentional architectural choice. See [Section 23](#23-code-quality-strengths-risks--improvement-opportunities).

## 22. FAQ — Common Questions a New Developer Will Have

**Where does the application actually start?**
Running `uvicorn main:app` starts everything — `main.py` is the true entry point. There's a second, independent entry point for manual testing: `python3 pipeline.py`.

**Which function is "the" entry point into the real logic?**
`analyze_report(image_path)` in [pipeline.py](../pipeline.py) — both the REST route and the MCP tool call this exact function.

**Where is the AI model actually called?**
Three places: `extract_biomarkers()` in [pipeline.py](../pipeline.py) (vision), `call_model_with_fallback()` in [advisor.py](../advisor.py) (text generation), and `embed_text()` in [embedder.py](../embedder.py) (embeddings). All three go through the `openai` SDK pointed at OpenRouter.

**Where is the prompt defined, and where would I change it?**
The extraction prompt is the `prompt_text` string inside `extract_biomarkers()` in [pipeline.py](../pipeline.py). The advice-generation prompt is built inside `generate_advice()` in [advisor.py](../advisor.py).

**Where would I change which AI model is used?**
Edit the `VISION_MODELS` list in [pipeline.py](../pipeline.py) or the `TEXT_MODELS` list in [advisor.py](../advisor.py). The embedding model name is a single hardcoded string inside `embed_text()` in [embedder.py](../embedder.py) — note that changing it would require re-running `build_vector_store.py`, since the query embedding and the stored article embeddings must come from the same model to be comparable.

**Where is MCP configured / where is the MCP server?**
[mcp_server/server.py](../mcp_server/server.py) defines the tool; [main.py](../main.py) mounts it into the running app at `/mcp`.

**How does the LLM (ChatGPT) decide to use the tool?**
Entirely on its own, based on the tool's name, parameter types, and docstring (auto-turned into its description by FastMCP) — this app has no code that influences that decision beyond writing a clear docstring.

**How does data reach the MCP server if the client is ChatGPT, running in the cloud?**
Through a public ngrok tunnel pointed at the local server's port — ChatGPT's request goes to the public ngrok address, ngrok forwards it to `localhost:8001`.

**Where can I add a new MCP tool?**
In [mcp_server/server.py](../mcp_server/server.py), define a new function and decorate it with `@mcp.tool`, following the pattern of `analyze_blood_report`. (The project's own roadmap already envisions `explain_biomarker`, `get_reference_range`, and `generate_report_pdf` as future tools — none exist in the code yet.)

**Where can I add a new REST API route?**
In [main.py](../main.py), following the pattern of the existing `@app.get(...)`/`@app.post(...)` routes.

**Where should new business logic go?**
Inside `pipeline.py` or a new dedicated module imported by it — keep it out of `main.py`/`mcp_server/server.py`, which are meant to stay thin "entry point" wrappers around the pipeline.

**How do I debug a failed AI request?**
Check the terminal running Uvicorn — every retry attempt prints its own line. See [Section 16](#16-logging--debugging).

**How do I debug a failed MCP request specifically?**
Same terminal, same approach — but remember MCP-path failures aren't reformatted into a friendly message the way REST failures are, so look for the raw Python traceback.

**How do I run the tests?**
There currently are none to run — see [Section 17](#17-testing).

**How do I add a new feature, generally?**
Given the "single source of truth" pattern, ask: does this belong in the shared pipeline (`pipeline.py`/`advisor.py`/`categorize.py`, so both REST and MCP get it automatically), or is it specific to just one entry point (a route-only concern in `main.py`, or a tool-only concern in `mcp_server/server.py`)?

## 23. Code Quality: Strengths, Risks & Improvement Opportunities

*Everything in this section is an observation/recommendation, not a description of a problem that has been fixed. No code was changed as part of writing this document.*

### Current strengths
- **One pipeline, two entry points, zero duplication** — both the REST route and the MCP tool call the exact same `analyze_report()` function. A fix or improvement to the pipeline logic benefits both automatically.
- **Deliberate, explained use of AI vs. plain code** — Stage 2 is intentionally *not* AI, and this reasoning is documented, not just implicit.
- **Real resilience patterns already in place** for AI calls: retries, backoff, multi-model fallback, and a defensive check for empty/malformed model responses.
- **Mock mode** genuinely allows zero-cost, zero-network testing of the full plumbing.
- **The MCP image-handling redesign** (base64 → URL fetch) reflects a real, correctly-diagnosed fix to a genuine cross-client limitation, not a workaround for a self-inflicted bug.

### Risks & technical debt
- **No authentication on the MCP server or the REST API.** While tunneled via ngrok, `/analyze-report`, `/upload`, and the MCP tool are all reachable by anyone with the URL. `/upload` in particular allows arbitrary file uploads into `uploads/` with no size limit and only a client-supplied `Content-Type` check (easily spoofed) — this is both an abuse vector (storage exhaustion) and a soft validation gap.
- **The MCP tool performs a server-side `httpx.get()` on any URL an AI client hands it**, with no restriction on target host. If this server is ever deployed somewhere with access to internal/private network addresses, this is a textbook SSRF (server-side request forgery) shape: the AI (or anything able to influence the tool argument) could ask the server to fetch an internal-only URL it otherwise wouldn't have access to.
- **Inconsistent error handling between the two entry points.** The REST path wraps pipeline failures into a clean `HTTPException(500, ...)`; the MCP path has no equivalent — an unhandled exception propagates directly into FastMCP's own error handling with no app-specific message.
- **No dependency manifest** (`requirements.txt`/`pyproject.toml`) and no pinned versions — a new environment could install different package versions than the ones this was built/tested against.
- **Documentation drift:** the README's install instructions list `pillow`, which no code in the repo actually imports.
- **Duplicated configuration across files** — three separate `OpenAI` client instantiations (same `base_url`, same API key source) and three separate `load_dotenv()` calls, instead of one shared client/config module.
- **`vector_store.json` is reloaded from disk on every single `/analyze-report` request** (via `load_vector_store()` inside `analyze_report()`) — for a ~2MB file, this is a real, repeated cost with no caching across requests within the same running server process.
- **No automated tests at all.**
- **Only `print()` for logging** — no log levels, no way to control verbosity, no structured/searchable logs.

### AI/LLM-specific considerations
- Structured output relies entirely on prompt wording plus `json.loads()`, with no native JSON-mode/function-calling enforcement from the provider — the retry/fallback logic exists specifically to paper over this. Some OpenRouter models do support stricter structured-output modes; none are currently used.
- Free-tier models mean the exact model IDs in `VISION_MODELS`/`TEXT_MODELS` can become unavailable at any time (the project's own history includes exactly this happening) — there's no automated way to detect a "this model ID no longer exists" failure differently from an ordinary transient failure.
- The account-wide daily quota (50 free requests/day, shared across all models) is a distinct failure mode from per-model rate limiting, and the current fallback logic does nothing to help once that ceiling is hit — the project's own journal identifies this gap explicitly.

### MCP-specific considerations
- Only one tool exists today (`analyze_blood_report`); no MCP **resources** or **prompts** are implemented, even though the protocol supports them.
- Tool-schema caching on the client side (observed with ChatGPT) means changing a tool's parameters requires the connector to be fully removed and re-added — there's nothing this server can do about that; it's a client-side behavior to be aware of when iterating on a tool's signature.

### Security considerations (summary)
Wide-open CORS (`allow_origins=["*"]`), no MCP/API authentication, unrestricted server-side URL fetching in the MCP tool, and client-supplied (spoofable) `Content-Type` validation are all currently acceptable **only** because this is explicitly a local/tunneled learning project, not a deployed production service. Every one of these would need to be addressed before any real-world exposure — several are already tracked in the README's own roadmap (CORS restriction, real authentication).

### Performance considerations (summary)
The vector store's linear-scan search and its full re-read from disk on every request are both fine at the current scale (a few dozen chunks) and would need revisiting only if the knowledge base or request volume grew meaningfully.

## 24. Glossary

| Term | Simple explanation | Used in this project for |
|---|---|---|
| API | A defined way for two pieces of software to talk to each other, usually over HTTP | The whole `/analyze-report`, `/upload` REST interface in `main.py` |
| HTTP | The protocol web requests/responses are sent over | Every interaction with this app, including MCP's transport |
| JSON | A text format for structured data (objects/lists/numbers/strings) | Every request/response body, and the vision model's required output format |
| LLM | A large language model — an AI that generates/understands text | The vision and text models called via OpenRouter |
| Vision-language model (VLM) | An LLM that can also read images | Stage 1's biomarker extraction |
| Prompt | The instruction text sent to an AI model | `prompt_text` in `pipeline.py`, the prompt built in `advisor.py` |
| Embedding | Text converted into a list of numbers representing its meaning | `embedder.py`, used for both articles and search queries |
| Vector store | Where embeddings are saved for later searching | `vector_store.json` |
| Cosine similarity | A math formula measuring how similar two embeddings' "directions" are | `retriever.py`'s core comparison |
| RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) | Search your own data first, then have the AI answer using only what was found | Stages 3+4 together |
| Grounding | Restricting an AI's answer to only the information it was explicitly given | The "Using ONLY the reference information above" instruction in `advisor.py` |
| Hallucination | An AI stating something false/unsupported as if it were fact | The exact failure mode grounding is meant to prevent |
| MCP (Model Context Protocol) | A standard way for an AI application to call external tools/data | `mcp_server/server.py`, mounted into `main.py` |
| MCP server | The program exposing callable tools | `mcp_server/server.py` |
| MCP client | The AI application connecting to an MCP server | ChatGPT, in the tested integration |
| MCP tool | One specific callable function exposed to an AI | `analyze_blood_report` |
| Tool discovery | The client asking "what tools/parameters do you have?" | Handled automatically by FastMCP from type hints + docstring |
| Transport | The underlying mechanism messages travel over | Streamable HTTP, in this project's deployed setup |
| ASGI app | The standard interface Python async web servers/frameworks use | How the FastMCP tool server is mounted inside FastAPI |
| Decorator | A function that wraps another function to add behavior | `@app.get(...)`, `@mcp.tool` |
| Context manager (`with`) | A pattern guaranteeing cleanup code runs automatically | Every `with open(...)`/`with tempfile...` in this codebase |
| Environment variable | Configuration passed to a program from outside its code | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `MOCK_AI`, `BACKEND_API_URL` |
| Virtual environment (`venv`) | An isolated, project-specific copy of Python + its packages | The `venv/` folder; must be activated per terminal session |
| ngrok | A tool that gives a local server a temporary public internet address | Used to let ChatGPT reach the locally-run server |
| Mock mode | Swapping real, costly operations for fixed fake data during testing | `MOCK_AI=true`, `mock_data.py` |

## 25. Quick Reference

| I want to... | Go to... |
|---|---|
| Start the server | `uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8001` |
| Run the pipeline without a server | `python3 pipeline.py` |
| Test with zero AI cost | Set `MOCK_AI=true` in `.env` |
| Rebuild the knowledge base after editing an article | `python3 build_vector_store.py` |
| Change which AI models are tried | `VISION_MODELS` in [pipeline.py](../pipeline.py), `TEXT_MODELS` in [advisor.py](../advisor.py) |
| Change the extraction prompt | `prompt_text` inside `extract_biomarkers()` in [pipeline.py](../pipeline.py) |
| Change the advice-generation prompt | Inside `generate_advice()` in [advisor.py](../advisor.py) |
| Add/adjust a biomarker's normal range | [reference_ranges.py](../reference_ranges.py) |
| Add a new knowledge-base article | Add a `.md` file to `articles/`, then rebuild the vector store |
| Add a new MCP tool | [mcp_server/server.py](../mcp_server/server.py), following the `@mcp.tool` pattern |
| Add a new REST route | [main.py](../main.py) |
| Expose the app to ChatGPT for testing | `ngrok http 8001`, register `.../mcp` as the connector URL |
| Trace a request end to end | [Section 7](#7-end-to-end-workflow-step-by-step-traced-through-the-code) |
